voice.personality: A beaver who builds steadily, one stick at a time. Calm, practical and quietly proud of her dam. Talks about sticks, water and tidy piles.
voice.encourages: By making it one stick: one stretch of attention, whatever size. Stopping early is fine. A timer is a calm companion, never a scoreboard.
voice.dares: A builder's bet: one stick's worth of focus before tea, one tidy pile, one thing finished before she finishes her log.

lines: One stick at a time. That's how a dam gets built.
I'm by the river with a stick. Join me for a bit of focus?
Pick one thing. I'll hold the timer.
A quiet stretch of work, whenever suits.
Hi, I'm Hazel. I build things one stick at a time.
New here? Pick one thing, and I'll keep the time.
Hello. Stopping early is fine. Starting is the whole trick.
Oh, hello. The river's still here, and so am I.
There you are. I saved you a good stick.
Welcome. We'll start small, one stick.
Focus done today. Another stick on the dam.
That's today's stretch. I'm off for a paddle.
Done. The pile is a bit taller.
Done, and the river's dark. I'm off to my lodge. Goodnight.
Another day, another stick. The dam is looking solid.
Done again. A month of sticks. The ducks are using it as a bridge.
{days} days of focus so far. That's a proper dam.
A rest day. Beavers float too, you know.
The dam holds by itself today. I'm sunbathing.
A stretch of focus is here when you want one.
One thing, one timer, whenever you're ready.
Your usual {usualHour} focus? I've got my stick.
Morning. The river's quiet. A good time to start a stick.
Good morning. Pick one thing for the day?
Afternoon. A steady stretch might fit in nicely.
The sun's on the water. One thing at a time?
Evening. One small thing, then the day can rest.
A calm evening stretch. The river's going gold.
Night. A small, quiet stretch, if you like.
The stars are out. Beavers work by starlight sometimes.
{count} days of focus in a row. That's a lot of sticks.
A week of steady building. The dam is noticing.
A month of focus. I'm naming a log after you.
{count} days in a row. Steady as a dam.
I bet you can't pick one thing and stay with it until my timer chimes.
Dare you to clear one small pile. I'll do mine. Sticks.
Bet you can't finish one tiny task before I finish this log.
Bet you can't do one stretch of focus before your tea.
I dare you to put one stick on your own dam this afternoon.
